full_judgment:
7. Mr. A.S.M. Wahidul Momin Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the appellate court committed an error of law in not believing the genuineness of the execution of the baina deed and payment of part of consideration money on the basis of the deposition of P.W. 1 the plaintiff and P.W. 3 Abdul Malik. He advanced further argument that in a case of this nature where the signatures are admitted by the defendant the onus shifts upon the defendant to prove that on receiving loan money he put his signature on a blank stamp paper and kept it with the plaintiff as security. In support of his submission he cited the case of Nasir Ahmed Khan Vs. Md. Ismat Jahan Begum, reported in 21 DLR(SC) 145. In further support he referred to section 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act submitting that when contents are reduced to writing in document, oral evidence as to the same is inadmissible. He also cited the case of Muhammedi Steamship Co. Ltd. and another Vs. Messrs, Doda Limited, Chittagong reported in 10 DLR 474. Mr Chowdhury as well drew my attention to the provision of Section 17 of the Evidence Act. I have gone through the decisions and read the provision of Section 17.91& 92 of the Evidence Act. Those are not applicable in this case, as because in this case the defendant does not admit the bainapatra vis-a-vis its contents. Defendant's plea is that he signed ma blank stamp paper which was kept as security against, loan received by him. So the above submissions of that learned Counsel does not inspire any confidence in me. The learned Counsel for petitioner also has cited decision in the case of Kambhan Lakshmanna Vs. Tangirals V chukatesh Warla, 2 DLR (PC) 83 and has repeatedly submitted that onus was in this case upon the defendant. The decision of their Lordships is very much noteworthy. Their Lordships have found that burden to prove shifts from stage to stage. In the instant case the defendant has discharged his initial onus by examining himself and some other witnesses. I find burden to prove heavily shifted upon the plaintiff to prove that he paid Tk. 35,000/- as part consideration and defendant signed the bainapatra on receiving the same. I find that the plaintiff has totally failed to discharge his onus. 

 "The fact that the defendant's thump impression appears on the paper is a strong piece of evidence in favour of the plaintiff and in the majority of cases very slight evidence would be necessary to prove that the thump impression was given on the document after it has been written out and completed. But the fact remains that if the evidence offered by the plaintiff to prove that the document was duly executed, or in other words, that the thump impression was given on the document after had been written out and completed, is found to be unreliable, cannot be deemed to have discharged the onus properly and no onus shifts upon the defendant merely by reason of the fact that the impression was given on a blank piece of paper."
